issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet antifreeze smell, coolant drips near the front of the engine, overheating, or milky oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 used lower intake gaskets that break down over time and leak coolant, either outside the engine or into the oil. It is the most-reported problem on the Venture, and GM issued bulletins with a revised gasket.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and watch the temperature gauge. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the gaskets replaced with the updated design before coolant contaminates the oil or the engine overheats.

issues.t: Overheating that leads to head gasket or cylinder head damage
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, steam or white exhaust smoke, a sweet smell, loss of heat, or rough running after the engine has overheated.
issues.why: Coolant loss, often from the intake gasket leak, lets the engine overheat. Running it hot can blow the head gaskets or crack a cylinder head.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as the gauge climbs. Have a combustion leak test done; fixing the coolant leak early avoids far bigger repairs.

issues.t: Automatic transmission jerking, hard shifts or failure
issues.sym: Jerking or banging into gear, harsh or erratic shifts, slipping, a whine at highway speed, loss of overdrive, or a check engine light with codes such as P1811 or P0742.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic suffers from a failing pressure control solenoid, worn clutches and valve body wear. GM issued several bulletins for firm shifts, shudder and slipping.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked as soon as shifting changes. A solenoid or valve body repair caught early can avoid a full rebuild.

issues.t: Shudder on the 1-2 shift
issues.sym: A shudder or chuggle when the van shifts from first to second under light acceleration, or firm shifts and no downshift when slowing.
issues.why: Wear in the transmission's second clutch and valve body. GM bulletins cover shudder and firm shifting on the 4T65-E used in these years.
issues.next: Have a transmission shop check for codes and confirm the cause before it gets worse.

issues.t: Power sliding door can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The power sliding door does not fully latch, or opens while the van is moving.
issues.why: Weak welds in the door's unlatch actuator could jam it so the door doesn't latch. GM recalled the vans (01V-067 and 01V-264) to inspect and replace the actuator.
issues.next: Keep kids buckled in and check the door is latched. Ask a dealer if both recall repairs were done.

issues.t: Power sliding door can push a passenger's arm (recall)
issues.sym: If a passenger holds the inside handle while the power door opens, their arm can be pulled into the seat back or armrest.
issues.why: The power sliding door motor keeps pushing even when a hand is on the handle. GM recalled the vans (04V-597) to change how the door works.
issues.next: Teach passengers not to hold the handle while the door opens. Check for an open recall with your VIN.

issues.t: Power sliding door won't open, close or latch
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops working, reverses while closing, looks closed but the alarm sounds when you shift out of Park, or rattles.
issues.why: Worn cables, the motor, the latch and door switches all fail with use. GM issued several bulletins on power sliding door operation.
issues.next: Use the door manually if you can. A shop can find whether the motor, cable or latch is at fault.

issues.t: Dead battery from power sliding door
issues.sym: The battery is dead after the van sits overnight or for a few days.
issues.why: On vans with power sliding doors, GM issued a bulletin for a battery drain linked to the door system.
issues.next: Have a shop do a parasitic draw test. Disconnecting the door's power system for a test can confirm the cause.

issues.t: Tapping noise from the engine
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire or loss of power.
issues.why: Owners traced it to loose rocker arm bolts or lifters coming out of place, which can lead to lost compression in a cylinder.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new tapping sound. Have the valvetrain checked early, before a loose part damages the engine.

issues.t: Dash gauges and fuel gauge read wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads low or empty with a full tank, the temperature gauge reads maximum, or the speedometer reads far too high.
issues.why: The instrument cluster fails, and on some vans the fuel level sensor gives bad readings. GM issued bulletins for inaccurate or fluctuating fuel gauges.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. Have the cluster and fuel sender tested to see which one is at fault.

issues.t: Fuel tank check valve can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell near the rear of the van, or wet spots on the side of the fuel tank.
issues.why: A weld on the fuel tank inlet check valve can crack and let fuel vapor and droplets escape, which could catch fire. GM recalled the vans (07V-349) and replaces the tank.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, have it checked right away and look up open recalls with your VIN.

issues.t: Steering can get hard to turn (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly takes much more effort, usually during left turns.
issues.why: The steering gear pinion shaft can move upward and drop back during turns. GM recalled the vans (02V-286).
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check for an open recall.

issues.t: Wiper linkage can rub a brake line (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking at the rear of the engine bay, a soft pedal or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: The windshield wiper linkage can rub against a brake line until it leaks. GM recalled the vans (98V-072) and issued a matching bulletin.
issues.next: Check for brake fluid leaks and have the recall checked. A soft brake pedal needs attention right away.

issues.t: Bucket seat release can injure fingers (recall)
issues.sym: Fingers can get caught when you release a removable bucket seat.
issues.why: The seat release mechanism could pinch or even cut off a finger if a hand is in the way. GM recalled the vans (98V-145).
issues.next: Keep hands clear when releasing seats, and check for an open recall.

issues.t: ABS or traction control light on
issues.sym: The ABS or traction control light comes on, sometimes on and off, and anti-lock braking may stop working.
issues.why: Wheel speed sensor and ABS module faults are the common causes. GM put out bulletins for ABS lights and wheel speed sensor diagnosis.
issues.next: Normal braking still works. Have the ABS codes read to find the faulty sensor or wire.

issues.t: Weak heat at idle in cold weather
issues.sym: The heater blows lukewarm air at idle or low speed in freezing weather.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for poor heater output at low engine speed below freezing, often helped by restoring full coolant level and flow.
issues.next: Make sure the coolant is full first, since a low level from a leak is a common cause. Then ask a shop about the GM bulletin fix.

issues.t: A/C weak in hot weather or noisy compressor clutch
issues.sym: The A/C feels weak on hot, humid days, or there is a rattle or noise from the compressor at 1,000–2,000 rpm.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for weak A/C in hot, humid weather and for compressor clutch noise.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and clutch checked rather than just adding refrigerant.

issues.t: Water leaks at the windshield or overhead console
issues.sym: Water drips from the overhead console or map light, or wet carpet after rain.
issues.why: Gaps in the windshield seal and around the roof console let water in. GM issued bulletins for these leaks.
issues.next: Dry the carpet to avoid mold and have a shop water-test and reseal the leak.

issues.t: Headlights fog up or lenses come loose
issues.sym: Moisture inside the headlights, dim lights, or a headlight lens falling off.
issues.why: The headlamp seals let water in and lenses can loosen. GM issued bulletins for leaking headlamps.
issues.next: Replace or reseal the headlamp so you can see well at night and the bulbs don't fail early.

issues.t: Power window switch fails
issues.sym: A power window won't go up or down from one or more switches.
issues.why: Power window switches commonly wear out on the Venture.
issues.next: Try the window from the driver's master switch to narrow it down, then replace the faulty switch.
